subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 5-month-old boy with cystic fibrosis and cholestatic liver disease is admitted with irritability and pallor. He has been fed a regular infant formula but receives no vitamin supplementation, and his stools are bulky and greasy. Examination shows scleral icterus, diminished vibratory sensation and proprioception in the lower extremities, absent ankle reflexes, and truncal ataxia. Hemoglobin is 7.4 g/dL with many acanthocytes on the peripheral smear.
question: Deficiency of which of the following vitamins best explains this infant's anemia and neurologic findings?
explanation_correct: Vitamin E (tocopherol and tocotrienol) is a lipid-soluble antioxidant that protects red cell and neuronal membranes from free radical damage. Deficiency in fat malabsorption, as in cystic fibrosis with cholestasis, causes hemolytic anemia with acanthocytosis and a demyelinating syndrome of the posterior columns and spinocerebellar tracts, with loss of proprioception and vibration sense and ataxia.

explanation_incorrect.B: Vitamin K deficiency produces a coagulopathy with prolonged prothrombin time; bleeding may cause anemia but not acanthocytes or a posterior column syndrome.
explanation_incorrect.C: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness, xerophthalmia, and squamous metaplasia of epithelia rather than hemolysis with acanthocytes.
explanation_incorrect.D: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy with gingival bleeding, perifollicular hemorrhage, and poor wound healing; hemoglobin falls only from blood loss.
explanation_incorrect.E: Vitamin B12 deficiency produces a megaloblastic anemia with hypersegmented neutrophils, an elevated methylmalonic acid level, and subacute combined degeneration, which is not accompanied by acanthocytosis or hemolysis.

educationalObjective: Vitamin E deficiency from fat malabsorption causes a hemolytic anemia with acanthocytes and a posterior column/spinocerebellar demyelinating syndrome that mimics Friedreich ataxia.
